questions.question:
Kube-bench reports that anonymous authentication is enabled on the API server.

On the control plane (`{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`) disable anonymous access to the API: unauthenticated requests to the API endpoints (`/api`, `/apis`, `/version`, ...) must be answered with HTTP 401. The kubelet probes the API server's `/livez` and `/readyz` endpoints **without credentials**, so these health endpoints must keep answering unauthenticated requests, and the kube-apiserver Pod must stay Ready.

Use the structured **AuthenticationConfiguration** (`--authentication-config` in the static Pod manifest `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml`; make the file available inside the Pod). Wait until the API server is healthy again.

verification.description: The kube-apiserver uses an AuthenticationConfiguration that disables anonymous access or limits it to the health endpoints
The running API server answers requests without credentials with HTTP 401 on /api, /apis and /version
The health endpoints still answer unauthenticated probes and the kube-apiserver stays Ready

questions.question:
In the namespace `cilium-lab` the Deployment `nginx` (Service `nginx`, port 80) is called by the Pods `curlpod` (label `app=curlpod`) and `other` (label `app=other`). There is no network policy yet.

Create a CiliumNetworkPolicy so that:

- the nginx Pods (`app=nginx`) accept ingress traffic on TCP port 80 **only from the Pods labelled `app=curlpod`**;
- that traffic requires **mutual authentication** (`authentication.mode: required`).

Afterwards `curlpod` must still reach the Service `nginx`, and the Pod `other` must not.

verification.description: A CiliumNetworkPolicy allows app=curlpod to app=nginx and requires mutual authentication
curlpod reaches nginx and Cilium holds a SPIRE authentication entry for both identities
Only curlpod may reach nginx: the Pod other is denied
The rule 'Detect dev mem access' has the requested priority, output and a condition on /dev/mem
Falco on {{NODE01}} raises the WARNING alert for a Pod that opens /dev/mem
The rule fires for /dev/mem only (not for /dev/mem2)

questions.question:
The cluster is meant to admit images through an **ImagePolicyWebhook**. The webhook backend runs on the control plane (`{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`) at `https://127.0.0.1:8443/image_policy`; it denies every image whose repository is under `untrusted/` (for example `docker.io/untrusted/app:1.0`) and allows all other images.

The configuration is in `/etc/kubernetes/admission/` on the control plane (`admission_config.yaml`, `kubeconf` and the CA `ca.pem`), but the API server does not apply the policy correctly yet:

- Fix the configuration so that the backend is reached. The policy must **deny the images if the backend cannot be reached** (fail closed).
- Enable the ImagePolicyWebhook admission plugin **in addition to the plugins that are already enabled**, point the API server to `/etc/kubernetes/admission/admission_config.yaml` and make the directory available inside the kube-apiserver static Pod.
- Wait until the API server is healthy again. Pods with other images must still be admitted in the namespace `image-gate`.

verification.description: kube-apiserver enables ImagePolicyWebhook (NodeRestriction kept) with the admission config; fail-closed and existing kubeconfig
Images from untrusted/ repositories are denied by the webhook
Pods with other images are still admitted (webhook reachable)

questions.question:
The manifest `/tmp/exam/mhagou-003-q5/pod.yaml` (on the jumphost) describes the Pod `web` of the namespace `kubesec-lab`. `kubesec` is installed on the jumphost.

Scan the manifest with `kubesec` and improve it by applying its recommendations until the score is **at least 12** and there is no critical advice. Keep the Pod name, the namespace and the image (`nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine`; it listens on port 8080 and writes temporary files to `/tmp`).

Then deploy the Pod from the improved manifest in `kubesec-lab`: it must run, as a non-root user and with a read-only root filesystem.

verification.description: The manifest scores at least 12 with kubesec, no critical advice, and is still the Pod web
The live Pod web runs, scores at least 12 and runs unprivileged with a read-only root filesystem

questions.question:
Istio is installed. The Service `helloworld` (port 5000) of the namespace `hello-mesh` runs with an Istio sidecar. The Pod `client` of the namespace `mesh-client` has **no** sidecar and calls it over plaintext.

1. Create a **mesh-wide** PeerAuthentication (the root namespace `istio-system`, no selector) that enforces **STRICT** mTLS.
2. Verify that the Pod `client` can no longer reach `http://helloworld.hello-mesh.svc.cluster.local:5000/hello`.
3. Make the `client` work again by bringing its namespace into the mesh: enable sidecar injection in `mesh-client` and recreate the Pod `client` so that it runs with the proxy.

Other plain clients (for example the Pod `plain` of the namespace `mesh-plain`) must stay unable to reach `helloworld`.

verification.description: A mesh-wide PeerAuthentication in istio-system requires STRICT mTLS
The client Pod runs with a ready Istio proxy and reaches helloworld
A client without a sidecar cannot reach helloworld over plaintext

questions.question:
The namespace `restricted-zone` runs a critical payment service (Deployment and Service `payment-service`, port 8000). Istio is installed. A legacy Pod without a sidecar (`legacy` in the namespace `legacy-zone`) exists.

1. Make sure that **all new Pods** of `restricted-zone` automatically get an Istio sidecar, and that the running `payment-service` Pods run with it as well.
2. Enforce **STRICT mTLS for the whole namespace** with a PeerAuthentication in `restricted-zone` (no selector, no exceptions).
3. Verify that the legacy Pod from `legacy-zone` cannot reach `payment-service`, while a Pod with a sidecar inside `restricted-zone` can.

verification.description: New Pods of restricted-zone get an Istio sidecar automatically
The running payment-service Pods have a ready Istio proxy
A namespace-wide STRICT PeerAuthentication without exceptions exists in restricted-zone
The legacy Pod is blocked and an injected client reaches payment-service

questions.question: Generate a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for the container image `nginx:1.19` in **SPDX** format with `trivy` (installed on the jumphost; `bom` and `syft` are not) and save it to `/tmp/exam/mhagou-003-q8/sbom.spdx`. Either SPDX JSON or SPDX tag-value is accepted.

verification.description: The file is an SPDX document with packages
The SBOM describes the image nginx:1.19
The SBOM lists the OS packages of the image (50 or more, nginx 1.19.x among them)

questions.question:
A critical application needs to be locked down.

1. Create the namespace **`secure-team`**. Enforce the **Baseline** Pod Security Standard on it (privileged Pods must be rejected) and make it **warn** about **Restricted** violations (Pods that only violate Restricted must still be accepted).
2. A seccomp profile is available on the worker nodes as `profiles/audit.json` (in `/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp`). Create the Pod **`nginx-secure`** (image `nginx`) in `secure-team` that uses this profile as a `Localhost` seccomp profile. The Pod must run.

verification.description: Namespace secure-team exists and is Active
secure-team enforces the baseline standard (a privileged Pod is rejected)
secure-team warns about restricted violations without rejecting the Pod
A Restricted-compliant Pod is accepted without warnings
Pod nginx-secure runs with the Localhost profile profiles/audit.json (Seccomp: 2)

questions.question:
In the namespace `token-lab` the ServiceAccount `token-bot` exists.

1. Create a ServiceAccount **token Secret** for `token-bot` (type `kubernetes.io/service-account-token`) and wait until it holds a token.
2. Create the Pod **`token-pod`** (image `nginx:alpine`) that uses `token-bot` and does **not** mount the default token automatically (`automountServiceAccountToken: false`).
3. Mount a **projected volume** read-only at `/var/run/secrets/custom-tokens` in the Pod with two sources: the token of the Secret (the key `token`, any file name) and a `serviceAccountToken` that **expires after 3600 seconds** (any file name).

verification.description: A ServiceAccount token Secret of token-bot exists and holds a token
Pod token-pod uses token-bot with automountServiceAccountToken false and no default token
The Secret token is projected at /var/run/secrets/custom-tokens and authenticates as token-bot
A projected serviceAccountToken with 3600 seconds lifetime is mounted there and is valid
